resources.string: Changes are not reapplied at boot. Android and the power HAL can adjust the limits while you use the phone. Frequencies are read from this device’s kernel.
Restore the frequency limits and online cores recorded when this app process first read them. The thermal switch is separate.
This cluster is offline or its frequency controls cannot be read.
Online · this core cannot currently be disabled
Change applied and verified. The system may subsequently adjust these values.
The requested CPU control is unavailable. Refresh the screen and try again.
The kernel no longer advertises that frequency. Choose one of the currently available values.
The minimum cannot exceed the maximum. Adjust the other limit first.
At least one core must remain online in each cluster.
The kernel rejected the change. The app attempted to restore the previous values.
The requested values did not remain applied. Another system component may have changed them. The app attempted to restore the previous values.
%1$s The previous values could not be fully restored. Check the values shown below or reboot.

Applying a range locks it in the kernel when supported. Android cannot replace it until you release the lock. CPU thermal frequency caps can also be bypassed; hardware limits still apply. Reboot releases the locks.
This kernel does not provide frequency locking. Install the kernel with Galaxian Parts support to force your limits. Changes here are temporary until then.
Android cannot replace this range. Turn off to return control to the system.
Android can adjust the limits. Turn on to hold the displayed range.
The selected CPU frequency range stays locked until you unlock it or restart the phone. This can override CPU frequency limits imposed by software temperature controls.
Frequency locking is unavailable in this kernel. Android can replace a temporary range.
